context.requirement_text:
Third and final part of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix, covering its own
explicitly-named SECONDARY surface: "Poller's per-tenant sweeps and
future LISTEN/NOTIFY work (ISS-0430) are secondary surfaces to cover
by the same decision rather than each inventing its own cap." Atop
REQ-216's core module; does not touch REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring.

WHAT `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` ACTUALLY DOES TODAY (read in
full, not assumed): `handle_info(:tick, ...)` calls
`Enum.each(schemas, fn schema_name -> Scheduler.poll_and_fire(schema_name)
end)` -- SEQUENTIAL, one tenant schema at a time, not concurrent. The
same sequential pattern repeats for
`maybe_run_retention_sweep/2`, `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`,
`maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`,
`maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1`. So THIS module does not exhibit
unbounded CONCURRENT demand the way the HTTP path does (each call
blocks the single Poller GenServer process, so at most one DB
connection is held by Poller work at any instant) -- the real gap
here is ACCOUNTING, not concurrency: Poller's one held connection is
invisible to REQ-216's admission budget, so REQ-216's global cap
(`pool_size - reserved_headroom`) can only be a safe ceiling on
HTTP-path concurrency if `reserved_headroom` already reserves enough
slack for Poller's own use -- an implicit, untested assumption today.
This requirement makes that assumption explicit and enforced rather
than merely documented.

SCOPE:
1. Before each of the six sequential per-tenant operations named
above (the timer poll-and-fire loop plus the five `maybe_run_*`
sweeps), acquire ONE global admission slot via
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)` for that operation's single
Repo-touching call, and release it immediately after that call
returns (success or the operation's own already-established rescue
path -- do not weaken any existing per-operation try/rescue
isolation boundary documented in poller.ex's moduledoc, e.g.
`maybe_run_alert_detection/3`'s own `rescue _ -> :ok`; the
acquire/release wraps around the existing isolation, it does not
replace it).
2. On `{:error, :capacity}` from `try_acquire(:global)` for a given
schema's operation within a tick: skip that one schema's operation
for that tick only (do not crash the GenServer, do not skip every
other schema's turn, do not skip that schema's OTHER operations this
tick if a later `try_acquire` call for a different operation
succeeds) -- mirroring `fetch_tenant_schemas/0`'s own existing
per-tick-degrades-gracefully philosophy already documented in this
module's moduledoc, applied per-schema-per-operation rather than
per-tick.
3. Poller does NOT use REQ-216's per-tenant semaphore -- only
`:global`. Reasoning: Poller's sweep already iterates every tenant
schema once per tick by design (REQ-186's own decision), so a
per-tenant CAP on Poller would not bound fairness between tenants the
way it does for bursty HTTP traffic, it would only cause a tenant to
be silently skipped some ticks for no client-visible reason -- a
strictly worse outcome for a background sweep whose whole contract is
"every tenant gets a turn." Stated explicitly rather than left
implicit.
4. No change to `Letflow.Application`'s supervision tree (no new
process; Poller remains the sole caller, same GenServer, same child
entry) and no change to `Letflow.Scheduler`'s own `poll_and_fire/1`
contract (unchanged input/output; the acquire/release wraps its call
site in `poller.ex`, per §1 above).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore or
REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring; no change to ISS-0430's future LISTEN/
NOTIFY work (named by ISS-0431 as a future secondary surface to cover
"by the same decision," not this requirement's own job to build); no
change to any `maybe_run_*` function's own internal per-schema
rescue logic beyond wrapping it in acquire/release.

task.description: WF-02 Step 3b hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's coverage for REQ-218. Independently re-derive AC-to-test mapping from docs/requirements.yaml's 6 authoritative ACs; scrutinize the new AC3(b) determinism claim with repeated foreground runs; verify AC4's grep is a real automated test; verify AC1's mock/spy-wording substitution is sound; check test/specs/REQ-218.md format against REQ-217.md/REQ-216.md; run the suite repeatedly in the foreground; time permitting, run a full-suite sanity check.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: forced-zero cap test present and its mock/spy-count substitution justified as equivalent
AC2: cap-of-1 sequential drain test present
AC3(a) and AC3(b) both present and each independently exercises its own sub-clause
AC4 is a real automated source-grep ExUnit assertion, not an informal handoff-quoted grep
AC5's rescue-path test genuinely forces a raise and proves the admission ref is released (after clause), not just the happy path
AC6: mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass, real output quoted
AC3(b)'s determinism mechanism (probe held before tick, deterministic first-call rejection, delayed release, 12 filler schemas) actually holds up under repeated runs, not merely claimed
test/specs/REQ-218.md format matches this project's established REQ-*.md spec conventions

ac_to_test_mapping_independently_rederiv.source_of_truth: docs/requirements.yaml lines 12940-12946 (REQ-218's acceptance_criteria list), read directly, not paraphrased from any handoff. Matches TEST-DESIGNER's step-04 quoted AC text verbatim -- confirmed no drift.
ac_to_test_mapping_independently_rederiv.AC1: describe "REQ-218 AC1: forced-zero admission cap skips every schema; capacity restored resumes normally" (poller_test.exs:479-507), 1 test. Verified Letflow.Admission.init/1 (lib/letflow/admission.ex:221-222) literally computes `global_cap = max(pool_size - reserved_headroom, 1)` -- confirms a literal 0 cap is structurally unreachable, so driving global_cap=1 plus a probe held before the tick is the only way to force 'every admission attempt this tick observes exhaustion', which is what AC1 actually needs. Mock/spy substitution verified sound: grepped mix.exs -- no mox/mock/meck dependency exists in this codebase, so a literal 'call count' assertion on Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 is unsatisfiable as worded; the test's substitute (3 schemas' due timers stay 'pending' while the probe is held, then all 3 flip to 'fired' after release on the next tick) is a real-effect assertion that is logically equivalent to a 0-then-3 call count, since poll_and_fire/1's only externally observable effect for a due timer IS that status transition. Read the test body directly -- confirmed non-vacuous.
ac_to_test_mapping_independently_rederiv.AC2: describe "REQ-218 AC2..." (poller_test.exs:509-527), 1 test: global_cap==1, no probe, 3 schemas' due timers all fire in one tick. Confirmed non-vacuous by reading the body directly.
ac_to_test_mapping_independently_rederiv.AC3: Two independent sub-clauses, confirmed both covered: (a) describe "REQ-218 AC3: a capacity rejection..." (poller_test.exs:570-602) -- 10-schema continuous-antagonist race, retried up to 5x for a genuine partial skip, proving a rejection for one schema's poll_and_fire does not block a DIFFERENT schema's SAME operation. (b) describe "REQ-218 AC3 (per-schema clause)..." (poller_test.exs:684-728) -- newly added, proving a rejection for a schema's poll_and_fire does not block that SAME schema's OTHER operations (retention sweep) later in the same tick. Confirmed via direct code read that (a) alone cannot exercise (b): (a)'s antagonist and assertions only ever look at poll_and_fire across many schemas, never at a second operation on the same schema, so a forbidden coarser design (one acquire/release per schema covering all six operations) would pass (a) but fail (b). Gap-close is genuine, not cosmetic.
ac_to_test_mapping_independently_rederiv.AC4: describe "REQ-218 AC4..." (poller_test.exs:734-742): `refute source =~ "{:tenant,"` against `File.read!("lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex")`. Confirmed this is a REAL, automated ExUnit assertion executed on every mix test run, not an informally-reported grep in a handoff -- it will fail the suite if a future edit reintroduces a `{:tenant, _}` call. Matches this file's own pre-existing 'no second ticker' test's precedent (poller_test.exs:774-787, grepping source text for `use GenServer`), confirming this is an established codebase convention, not a one-off shortcut. Cross-checked poller.ex's actual source directly -- confirmed zero `{:tenant,` occurrences; all 6 with_admission/3 call sites pass only `:global` to Admission.try_acquire/1 (poller.ex:165).
ac_to_test_mapping_independently_rederiv.AC5: describe "REQ-218 AC5..." (poller_test.exs:744-772). Read the test body and poller.ex's with_admission/3 (poller.ex:164-181) together: the acquire/release IS structured as `case ... {:ok, ref} -> try do fun.() after Admission.release(ref) end`, so the `after` clause is the ONLY release mechanism regardless of whether fun.()'s own inner rescue fires. The test forces a genuine raise (drops effect_completions, triggering maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1's own `rescue _ -> :ok` at poller.ex:288-292, itself wrapped inside with_admission/3), then asserts (a) the tick does not crash the caller, (b) a DIFFERENT intact schema's own timer still fires (no total-tick poisoning), and (c) a post-tick probe try_acquire(:global) still succeeds under global_cap==1 -- which would fail if the raised call's ref had leaked. This genuinely exercises the after-clause's specific purpose (belt-and-suspenders past an inner rescue, and the SOLE release path for poll_and_fire/retention which have no inner rescue at all) -- not vacuous, not merely the happy path.
ac_to_test_mapping_independently_rederiv.AC6: Verified directly below (own foreground runs), not merely by trusting TEST-DESIGNER's quoted transcript.

ac3b_scrutiny.mechanism_confirmed: Read ac3b_attempt/3 (poller_test.exs:651-682) and its surrounding comment (lines 615-650) in full, cross-checked against poller.ex's actual Enum.each ordering (handle_info/2, poller.ex:124-153): the timer poll-and-fire loop over `schemas` runs FIRST, before maybe_refresh_active_instances/1, maybe_run_retention_sweep/2, and the three ordering passes. The test's probe try_acquire(:global) happens in the TEST process, synchronously, before Poller.handle_info(:tick, state) is even called -- same-process happens-before guarantees this schema's poll_and_fire admission attempt (the tick's structurally first admission call) is deterministically rejected, no race on that side. Confirmed clear_pending_events!/1 (line 611-613) is called at the start of every attempt, closing the cross-attempt event-leakage bug TEST-DESIGNER's own account describes. Confirmed 12 filler schemas (line 713) are provisioned once outside the retry loop and reused, widening the real DB round-trip gap between the target schema's own two admission attempts (its poll_and_fire near the very start of the tick, its retention sweep only after the ENTIRE poll_and_fire loop plus the unwrapped maybe_refresh_active_instances pass over every schema complete) -- this structurally removes exactly the antagonist-timing bias TEST-DESIGNER's own account says the first two failed drafts exhibited (a continuous two-sided antagonist race, and a design that let a rejected attempt's own event get swept up by a later attempt).
ac3b_scrutiny.own_repeated_runs: Ran `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs --only describe:"REQ-218 AC3 (per-schema clause): a rejected schema's other ops still proceed"` 20 CONSECUTIVE times in the foreground (own shell, own PIDs, not reused from TEST-DESIGNER's report). Every single run printed `Result: 1 passed, 12 excluded` -- 20/20 passed, 0 failures, 0 flakes observed. This independently corroborates TEST-DESIGNER's own reported 20/20 isolated-run result rather than just re-reading their claim.
ac3b_scrutiny.verdict: The determinism argument holds up under independent, repeated, foreground scrutiny. Not treated as flaky.

result.summary: PASS. Independently re-derived the AC-to-test mapping directly from docs/requirements.yaml's 6 authoritative acceptance criteria and confirmed every one has genuine, non-vacuous coverage. AC3's two independent sub-clauses are each covered by their own dedicated test, and the gap TEST-DESIGNER found (the existing suite could not distinguish the shipped per-operation design from a forbidden coarser per-schema design) is real and correctly closed by the new AC3(b) test. Scrutinized AC3(b)'s determinism claim (probe held before the tick for a deterministic first-admission rejection, delayed release, 12 filler schemas to widen the real timing window) by reading the mechanism against poller.ex's actual Enum.each ordering, and independently re-ran it 20 consecutive times in the foreground myself (not reusing TEST-DESIGNER's reported counts) -- 20/20 passed, 0 failures, corroborating the determinism argument rather than just trusting the report. AC4 is confirmed to be a real, automated ExUnit source-grep assertion matching an established codebase convention, not an informal handoff-quoted grep. AC1's mock/spy-count wording substitution is confirmed sound: no mocking library exists in this codebase (grepped mix.exs), Admission.init/1's own `max(pool_size - reserved_headroom, 1)` floor makes a literal 0 cap unreachable, and the substituted real-effect assertion (timers stay pending under the probe, then all fire once released) is logically equivalent to the 0-then-3 call-count fact the AC describes. AC5 genuinely forces a raise through an existing rescue path and proves the wrapping `after` clause released the admission ref (post-tick probe still succeeds), not just the happy path. test/specs/REQ-218.md's structure and section conventions match test/specs/REQ-217.md and REQ-216.md exactly. Own foreground runs: mix compile clean (0 warnings), 20/20 isolated AC3(b) passes, 3/3 full-file runs at 13/13 passed each, and one full independent `mix letflow.check.test` run (3139/3141 passed, 2 pre-existing environment-only rustc-toolchain failures confirmed by name and by directly checking rustc is absent from this host's PATH, 0 REQ-218 failures, 0 ISS-0069 regressions). No gaps found; no fixtures depend on shared hardcoded state (restart_admission!/1 registers its own on_exit restore); no test requires another test to have run first; no skipped tests; no hardcoded secrets.
